originalTitle: Quote of the day by John Templeton: "I have learned that the great opportunities are the places that have been neglected, where other people are not looking"
simplifiedContent: John Templeton, a well-known investor, believes that the best investment opportunities are often found in areas that others are not paying attention to. He thinks that instead of following what's currently popular, investors should look for companies or investments that have good basics but are being overlooked. This approach requires investors to do their own research, be patient, and think about the long term. By doing so, they may be able to find investments that are undervalued before they become widely popular. This philosophy can help investors make smart decisions and potentially find great opportunities that others are missing.

originalTitle: Market wrap: TCS, Eternal, HUL, BEL among top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Tuesday
simplifiedContent:
Here's a simplified version of the news: 
The Indian stock market ended slightly lower on Tuesday, even though it started the day with some gains. This happened because some technology companies like TCS did well, but other types of companies, such as those that make consumer goods, didn't do as well. As a result, the market didn't go up as much as it could have. Experts think the market will stay steady for now, with some important numbers to watch: if it goes above 24,050, that's a good sign, and if it goes below 23,800, that's a bad sign. This information can help investors make decisions about what to do with their money.

originalTitle: L&T Q1 Results: Net profit rises 14% YoY to Rs 4,123 crore, revenue up 7%
simplifiedContent: Larsen & Toubro, a big company, just shared its financial results for the first three months of the year. The company made a profit of Rs 4,123 crore, which is 14% more than it made during the same time last year. This means the company is doing better than it was a year ago. The company's overall income, or revenue, also increased by 7% compared to last year. This is good news for investors, as it shows the company is growing and making more money.

originalTitle: Expert view: 10 sectors that could generate alpha over the next 5–10 years, according to Right Horizons PMS founder
simplifiedContent: Anil Rego, the founder of Right Horizons PMS, has shared his expert opinion on which areas of the stock market could do well over the next 5-10 years. He has identified 10 sectors that have the potential to perform better than others, even if the overall market is uncertain. Rego also expects the Nifty, a key stock market index, to see its earnings grow by around 12% per year from FY26 to FY28. This growth rate is measured as a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), which means it's the rate at which the earnings are expected to grow each year. This information matters because it can help investors make informed decisions about where to put their money.

originalTitle: US stock market today: Wall Street edges lower as chip stocks face fresh sell-off; Brent slips below $85
simplifiedContent: The US stock market is expected to start the day with lower prices. This is because companies that make computer chips, like Micron Technology, are seeing their stock prices drop due to concerns about how much money is being spent on artificial intelligence. As a result, the Nasdaq-100 futures, which track the performance of major tech stocks, have fallen by 0.9%. Micron Technology's stock price has dropped by 4.5%, which is a significant decline. This matters because it could affect the overall performance of the stock market and the value of investments in tech companies.

originalTitle: Mint Explainer | Why Sebi is overhauling online dispute resolution
simplifiedContent: Sebi, which is like a referee for the stock market, is planning to make big changes to how it handles disputes online. Right now, when investors have problems, they can file complaints online, but Sebi wants to make this process faster and more effective. To do this, Sebi is going to give some of the responsibility for handling these complaints to other organizations that help run the stock market. This change is meant to help resolve investor complaints more quickly and make sure that everyone is held accountable. This matters because it could help make the stock market a fairer and more trustworthy place for individual investors.
